Text: In this demo a Day Pass (modelled on a single-day ticket bundle) admits the holder to public screenings and Q&As on the day printed on it. It does not admit to Offscreen talks, industry office hours, press & industry screenings or Awards night.
A Single Film Ticket ($37) admits one person to the one screening named on it, including any Q&A that follows. Single tickets go on sale January 8, 2027 at 10 a.m. MT.

In this demo a Festival Pass (modelled on the Full Festival Ticket Package and Express Passes) admits the holder to public screenings, Q&As and Offscreen talks on every festival day, January 21 to 31, 2027. It does not admit to industry office hours, press & industry screenings or Awards night.
A VIP pass (donor level) admits the holder to public screenings, Q&As, Offscreen talks and Awards night on every day.

An industry (SIO) credential admits the holder to public screenings, Q&As, talks and industry office hours at the Festival HQ, The Rink. Credentials are picked up at The Rink: Wed Jan 20 2–7 p.m.; Thu Jan 21 to Tue Jan 26 8 a.m.–6 p.m.; Wed Jan 27 to Fri Jan 29 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; Sat Jan 30 9 a.m.–1 p.m. Bring photo ID.

A press credential admits the holder to public screenings, Q&As, talks and press & industry (P&I) screenings at Cinemark Century Boulder, 1700 29th St. P&I screenings run January 21 to 27, with repeats through January 29. P&I screenings have no intros, Q&As or audience voting.
A panelist badge admits the holder to all talks, public screenings and Q&As, and to Awards night.
A filmmaker credential admits the holder to all public screenings, Q&As, talks, industry office hours and Awards night.

A volunteer credential admits the holder to the venue of their shift, from 30 minutes before the shift starts until it ends. It is not an audience pass. Volunteers can use film vouchers in the staff and volunteer line or the public waitlist.
A festival staff badge admits the holder to every venue and event.

All tickets are digital QR codes in the Sundance Film Festival 2027 app, on the web under My Schedule, or in Apple or Google Wallet. No physical tickets are issued. Single tickets are fully transferable until used; package holders can change a selection up to 4 hours before the screening.
Ticket holders must be in line 15 minutes before the published start time, or admission depends on available seats. Late entry after the start is at theatre staff's discretion if space is available.

All seating is general admission, first come first seated; there is no reserved seating. Lines form about 1 hour before showtime and the house opens about 30 minutes before. Groups are seated only when everyone in the party is present.

The e-Waitlist is joined in the app or on the website, never in person. It opens 2 hours before showtime and closes 30 minutes before. You get a numbered position and may add one companion. Empty seats are sold to the waitlist line at the start of the screening; a card must be on your account.

The Sundance Film Festival 2027 runs 11 days, Thursday January 21 to Sunday January 31, 2027, in Boulder, Colorado, its first year in Boulder. World premieres run January 21 to 26; encore screenings run January 22 to 31. Jury and audience awards are announced Friday January 29, and award-winner screenings follow on January 30 and 31.

The Information Hub & Box Office is at the Downtown Boulder Visitor Information Center, 1303 Pearl Street. It is open Monday January 18 to Saturday January 30, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., and Sunday January 31, 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. It is the only place at the festival that accepts cash. Venue box offices open one hour before the first screening of the day.

Your tickets are QR codes in the Sundance Film Festival 2027 app under My Tickets & Passes. A ticket admits you to a screening; your separate Festival ID QR code admits you to events such as Offscreen talks.

Every title has at least one open-captioned screening, and closed-caption devices are available at every other screening. Assistive listening devices are available at all festival theatres. Wheelchair spaces are limited, with three companion seats per space; request them in advance at accessibility@sundance.org or (435) 776-7790. ASL is offered at select talks and Q&As. Service animals only.

All sales are final. If an in-person screening is cancelled because of an act of nature or a technical issue, single-ticket holders get a refund or an exchange. Processing fees are never refunded. Volunteers cannot issue refunds.
Bags and jackets are checked at every official venue, and some venues use metal detectors. Luggage and duffel bags are not allowed and cannot be stored at any venue.
Theatre rules: phones off, no recording, no babies in arms or strollers, and no pets except service animals. Water refill stations are at every venue.

Boulder in late January averages a high of about 47°F and a low of about 22°F, with about 12 inches of snow in the month. Sunrise is about 7:15 a.m. and sunset about 5:10 p.m. Dress in layers with a hat, gloves and warm boots. Chautauqua Auditorium has an outdoor line only. Scooters and e-bikes run unless there is more than a foot of snow.
Audience voting needs a scanned ticket or pass. Vote in the app with a 4-star rating, once per screening. A reminder arrives 1 hour before the scheduled end of the screening.

Screenings: Macky Auditorium (2,036 seats), Chautauqua Auditorium (about 1,300), Boulder Theater (850), Boulder High School Auditorium, Roe Green Theatre (412), Muenzinger Auditorium (400), Casey Middle School Auditorium, the Dairy Arts Center (Gordon Gamm 244, Grace Gamm 112, Boedecker 68), eTown Hall and Cinemark Century Boulder. Offscreen talks: Canyon Theater at the Main Library (190) and Old Main. Festival HQ is The Rink, 1722 14th St. All venues are within about 2 miles.

Buses between all Boulder venues are free during the festival through the City of Boulder and RTD. HOP loops downtown, CU, University Hill and Twenty Ninth Street from 6 a.m. to 2:30 a.m.; SKIP (Broadway), JUMP (Arapahoe) and BOLT are also free. The temporary CHAT route runs to Chautauqua every 10 minutes from 8 a.m. to midnight. Local buses run every 10 to 15 minutes.

There is no public parking at festival venues; park once. In city downtown garages the first 2 hours are free, then $20 flat, on Jan 21–24 and Jan 29–31; other days pay regular rates. CU visitor garages charge $20 a day. RTD Park-n-Rides are free for in-district cars for 24 hours.

Boulder is about 45 minutes from Denver International Airport. RTD AB1 runs from DEN to Downtown Boulder Station in about 65 minutes for a $10 Airport Day Pass. The Flatiron Flyer from Denver Union Station takes about 57 minutes and runs until 2 a.m. during the festival.

The City plans up to 5,000 free shared e-bike passes. Lime scooters and seated gliders are available, with extra stations for the festival. Rideshare pick-up and drop-off areas are designated near each venue.

Boulder Theater to eTown Hall is about 3 minutes on foot; downtown to the CU venues about 15 to 20 minutes; the four CU venues are within a 10-minute walk of one another; the Dairy and Cinemark are about 10 minutes apart. Chautauqua is about 30 to 40 minutes uphill from downtown, so take CHAT.

Clock in and out in the Bloomerang Volunteer app, with the QR code on your credential, or at the kiosk. Arrive 30 minutes before your shift and check in with the house manager at your venue. Volunteer check-in runs January 16 to 31.
Scan every QR code. If the scanner shows red, read the reason aloud and send the person to the box office or info desk. Do not override a red scan; only a house manager can make an exception.
Keep the ticket line, the Express line and the e-Waitlist line apart. Ticket holders must be in line 15 minutes before start. At the start time, empty seats go to the waitlist line in number order.
Lost items are held at each venue during the day, then taken to the Festival HQ at The Rink, 1722 14th St.

In an emergency call 911, then venue security, then the house manager. The trauma centre is Boulder Community Health Foothills Hospital, 4747 Arapahoe Ave. Do not post about incidents on social media.
Shift changes go through the volunteer team; the drop deadline was January 3, 2027. Contact volunteers@sundance.org or (435) 776-7870.
